strengths.title: The paper is unusually candid about the limits of its own central claim
strengths.why: Section 3.4 volunteers that "Faithfulness is thus artifact-relative: upstream biases, such as residual structural-compactness correlation (Section 5.1), propagate into the chains and are documented," and Section 6 restates it as a named limitation alongside "Single-source training corpus. Pico-Banana is generated by one text-conditioned editor, so Stage B masks reflect that editor's artifact statistics." Authors have every incentive to let "auditable" and "grounded" go unqualified; qualifying them in two places, and naming the human-audit set as the missing piece, is the right scholarly instinct and should be credited even while the same qualification undercuts the priority claim.

strengths.title: Appendix A documents concrete, transferable defects in the upstream corpora that a re-user would otherwise rediscover the hard way
strengths.location: Appendix A, Pico-Banana and MagicBrush adapters (p. 12)
strengths.why: "the integer-only parse produced ~22% duplicate IDs on the full release"; "the mask_img field is an RGB image where the edited region is painted pure black ([0,0,0]) over the target image's color content. The naive 'convert(L)>127' threshold inverts the mask"; "Sets metadata['source_is_authentic'] = True only for turn_index == 1; for turns >= 2 the 'source' is itself a previously edited image." These are exactly the details that silently corrupt derived work and that almost never make it into papers. Each is a real finding about two widely used datasets, and together they substantiate the pipeline half of the contribution in a way the dataset half is not substantiated.

strengths.title: The limitations section is candid and self-damaging in the right way, including a reported negative follow-up result
strengths.location: §6 Limitations (p9), six bullets; §5.4 "Effect of additional training" (p8)
strengths.why: The authors state limits that actively weaken their own pitch rather than hedging them. "Artifact-relative faithfulness. Chains are auditable against upstream masks, difficulty scores, and category labels, but these artifacts are themselves outputs of computational stages" concedes that the paper's central claim of grounding is relative, not absolute. "Unverified inference-time chain faithfulness... generated triplet-grounded statements are model estimates rather than verified quantities" concedes that the trained model does not inherit the property the dataset is built around. And §5.4 reports a failed follow-up in full: "chain-target regresses: spatial extraction recall drops 79.9→67.0%, and conditional spatial/bin accuracy falls from 37.2→32.5% and 40.8→34.4%." Reporting an experiment that went the wrong way, with numbers, is the behaviour the checklist's limitations guideline is trying to elicit and most submissions do not.

strengths.title: Appendix A documents exactly the non-obvious source-format failure modes a re-implementer would otherwise rediscover the hard way
strengths.location: Appendix A, Stage A source-dataset adapters (p12)
strengths.why: Three concrete, checkable gotchas are written down: the MagicBrush mask polarity trap — "the mask_img field is an RGB image where the edited region is painted pure black ([0,0,0]) over the target image's color content. The naive 'convert(L)>127' threshold inverts the mask"; the Pico-Banana identifier collision — "the integer-only parse produced ∼22% duplicate IDs on the full release"; and the multi-turn provenance flag — "Sets metadata['source_is_authentic'] = True only for turn_index == 1; for turns ≥2 the 'source' is itself a previously edited image." That last one is a real forensic-validity hazard that the authors identified and handled rather than silently inheriting. This is the most reproducibility-useful content in the paper and it partially offsets the missing code.

strengths.title: Appendix C gives a runnable command with concrete arguments and states honestly what the tool cannot do
strengths.why: The paper supplies the literal invocation — "uv run python scripts/sweep_global_threshold.py paths.masks_parquet=... candidate_thresholds=[0.50,...,0.64]" — the output schema ("a CSV report with columns (threshold, path1_global_rate, n_total)"), and a plainly stated limitation: "What the tool does not simulate is Path 2 (the post-Otsu area-based promotion to global). Path 2 requires the binarized mask, which is not retained in Stage B's per-triplet record. The reported Path-1 rate is therefore a lower bound." Naming a bound as a bound, and explaining the storage reason for it, is a level of methodological honesty about tooling that is uncommon.

strengths.title: The supervision targets themselves are made fully inspectable in the paper, and are version-stamped for downstream auditability
strengths.location: Appendix B / Table 4 (p13); Appendix D per-category chain examples (pp14–17)
strengths.why: All 12 forensic-prior templates are printed in full, and one complete Stage E output is shown verbatim per category — "Each example is a Stage E output verbatim." The templates are versioned and the version travels with the data: "Templates are versioned (TEMPLATE_VERSION = 'v1.0'); the version is recorded in each chain's structured header for downstream auditability." Because of this, a reader can evaluate the quality and the hedging discipline of the released text ("Edits of this type typically exhibit...") without the artifact in hand. Given that no link is provided, this transparency is the only reason the dataset's character is assessable at all — and version-stamping generated supervision is a practice more dataset papers should copy.

strengths.title: Where a statistical test is run, it is fully and correctly specified
strengths.why: "improving MagicBrush dev IoU by 1.3 points over the best two-signal subset (paired bootstrap p <10−4, 95% CI [0.0085,0.0164])" names the test, states that it is paired, gives both the p-value and a two-sided interval on the effect size, and reports the comparison against the strongest alternative rather than the weakest. This is exactly what the checklist's item-7 guideline asks for. The defect is that this rigour was not extended to Tables 2 and 3, not that it is absent from the paper.

strengths.title: The dual-use risk is named specifically and self-implicatingly rather than as boilerplate
strengths.why: "such detectors could suppress legitimate creative work or intensify an arms race in which generators learn to avoid the forensic cues encoded in our templates" identifies a concrete mechanism by which this particular artifact — not generative AI in general — could cause harm, and points at the authors' own Appendix B templates as the vector. Most broader-impact sections at this venue restate generic deepfake concerns; this one reasons about the specific object being released. The mitigation offered does not follow from it (recorded as a separate finding), but the risk identification itself is genuine work.
